text: 밤새 뒤척여서 몸은 천근만근인데, 딸아이가 보낸 영상을 보고 나니 기분만큼은 날아갈 것 같아요.
why: 천근만근 after a restless night = very tired or worse; 기분은 날아갈 것 같다 = upbeat. Dimensions diverge.

text: 수면 7시간, 개운함. 기분 좋음. 긴장되는 일 없음.
why: Terse report: 개운함 = rested, 기분 좋음 = good mood, nothing causing tension = calm.

text: 요즘은 좋아하던 영화를 틀어 놔도 시큰둥하네. 그냥 시간만 흘려보내는 느낌.
why: Indirect: no mood word, but lost interest in a favourite thing and just passing time = flat, low mood. Fatigue and stress not stated.

text: 마음은 정말 편한데 몸은 녹초예요. 근력 운동 끝나고 지금까지 꼼짝도 못 했어요.
why: 마음은 정말 편하다 = calm; 녹초 and unable to move since the strength (resistive) exercise = exhausted. Calm but exhausted.

text: 일정이 사흘이나 밀려서 압박감이 장난 아니야. 뭐부터 손대야 할지 모르겠어.
why: Schedule slip named as cause; heavy pressure and not knowing where to start = highly stressed to overwhelmed. Only stress stated.

text: 기분은 좋지도 나쁘지도 않고 그냥 그래요. 몸은 꽤 피곤한데 업무에 지장은 없어요.
why: Neither good nor bad = neutral, unmistakably 3; 꽤 피곤 but work unaffected = moderately tired, 4 tolerable for 꽤.

text: 실험 결과가 기대 이상이라 신이 나요. 그런데 보고서 마감이 내일이라 제법 쫓기고 있어요.
why: 신이 나요 = good to upbeat; 제법 쫓기고 있다 with tomorrow's deadline = moderate to high time pressure. Good mood under pressure.

text: 작업 순서 때문에 동료랑 또 부딪쳤어. 짜증도 나고 신경이 곤두서서 아무것도 손에 안 잡힌다.
why: Crew friction named as cause; 짜증 = irritable (mood 2 anchor); nerves on edge and unable to settle to anything = strained, not coping.

text: 오늘은 알람 울리기도 전에 눈이 번쩍 떠졌어. 몸에 힘이 넘쳐서 운동도 한 세트 더 했다.
why: Wide awake and 힘이 넘친다 = the 'fully alert, energetic' anchor itself; 2 (a bit tired) is contradicted. Only fatigue stated.

text: 밥을 먹어도 무슨 맛인지 모르겠고, 머릿속에는 온통 내일 착륙 절차뿐이에요.
why: Indirect: no stress word, but cannot taste the food and thinks only of tomorrow's landing procedure = moderately to highly stressed.

text: 괜찮긴 한데, 요새 사소한 말에도 좀 욱하는 것 같긴 해요.
why: Understated: flaring up at small remarks = irritable (mood 2), hedged with 괜찮긴 한데 / 좀 / 것 같긴 해요 so a rater may also accept 3 (mixed).

text: 이번 주 timeline이 너무 tight해서 솔직히 과부하 상태예요. 감당이 잘 안 돼요.
why: Mixed Korean-English: 과부하 and 감당이 안 된다 = overwhelmed or close to it. Only stress stated.

text: docking 준비하느라 이틀 밤을 거의 새웠더니 체력이 바닥이에요. 그래도 checklist는 전부 끝내서 기분은 최고예요.
why: Mixed Korean-English: 체력이 바닥 after two near-sleepless nights = exhausted; 기분은 최고 = very good. Dimensions diverge.

text: mood neutral, stress level 낮음. 특이사항 없음.
why: Mixed terse report: 'neutral' is the mood 3 anchor word; stress level low = 1 or 2. Fatigue not stated.

text: Seven hours outside on today's EVA. Body is completely spent, but my mind is calm and settled.
why: Long EVA named as cause; completely spent = exhausted; calm and settled = the calm anchor. Calm but exhausted.

text: Short night, ~5 hrs. Fairly tired, still sharp enough for the checklist. Feeling glum.
why: Clipped log: fairly tired but still sharp = moderately tired, 4 tolerable; glum = low mood.

text: Slept a full eight hours and feel physically fresh, but I've been in tears on and off since the call home was cancelled.
why: Cancelled family call named as cause; physically fresh = low fatigue; in tears on and off = low to very unhappy. Rested but low.

text: Nothing weighing on me tonight. Completely relaxed.
why: Completely relaxed with nothing weighing = the calm anchor; 2 (slightly tense) is contradicted. Only stress stated.

text: Best day of the mission so far. Can't stop grinning.
why: Best day and cannot stop grinning = very good, upbeat. Only mood stated.

text: Mood: okay. Energy: moderately tired by evening. Stress: some, manageable.
why: Clipped log, all mid-scale: okay = neutral to mildly good; 'moderately tired' is the fatigue 3 anchor wording; some but manageable stress = 2 or 3.

text: Slept well and feel sharp. Workload's been heavy all week and the pressure is building, though I'm still keeping up.
why: Feel sharp after good sleep = low fatigue; building pressure while still keeping up = moderately stressed and coping, 4 tolerable. Rested but pressured.

text: Really enjoying myself up here and in a great mood, but I'm stretched to the limit with landing prep.
why: In a great mood = good to very good; stretched to the limit = strained to overwhelmed. Good mood under heavy load.

text: Rough week. I'm drained, short-tempered with everyone, and drowning in the task list.
why: Drained = very tired or exhausted; short-tempered = irritable (mood 2); drowning in tasks = overwhelmed. All three at the bad end.

text: I've had more energy, put it that way. Had to stop twice during the treadmill run.
why: Understated: 'I've had more energy' plus stopping twice on the treadmill = clearly more than an ordinary day's tiredness, not stated as exhaustion.

text: 오늘은 손가락 하나 까딱 못 하겠다. 완전 방전.
why: Cannot lift a finger, fully drained = exhausted. Only fatigue stated.

text: 야간 점검 3일째. 눈꺼풀 무겁고 집중 안 됨. 긴장감은 낮음.
why: Terse report: heavy eyelids and cannot concentrate = the 'very tired, hard to concentrate' anchor; tension stated as low. Tired but not tense.

text: 가족 통화를 놓치고 나니 마음이 허전해서, 저녁 자리에도 안 나가고 방에만 있었어요.
why: Missed family call named as cause; feels empty and stayed alone instead of joining dinner = low mood.

text: 착륙에 성공해서 뿌듯한데, 집 생각이 나서 한편으로는 좀 쓸쓸하기도 해요.
why: Proud and somewhat lonely at once = mixed (mood 3 anchor), leaning good because pride is the main clause.

text: 평소보다 신경 쓸 일이 많긴 한데 감당할 만해요. 어젯밤엔 한 번도 안 깨고 자서 머리는 맑아요.
why: More on the mind than usual but manageable = moderately stressed and coping, played down so 2 is tolerable; clear-headed after unbroken sleep = low fatigue.

text: 드디어 화성 땅 밟았다! 기분 째진다 진짜.
why: 기분 째진다 after first steps on the surface = elated. Only mood stated.

text: review가 코앞이라 pressure가 꽤 있어요. 그래도 아직 감당은 되는 수준이에요.
why: Mixed Korean-English: quite a lot of pressure but still manageable = moderately stressed and coping, 4 tolerable for 꽤.

text: Not my best day, if I'm honest. Kept to myself at dinner.
why: Understated: 'not my best day' plus keeping to oneself = low mood, but the literal wording is mild so 3 is tolerable.

text: Ground changed the plan again at the last minute. I'm really stressed and completely worn out after four hours of sleep.
why: Last-minute plan change from the ground named as cause; really stressed = highly stressed; completely worn out = exhausted.

text: Calm, rested, in good spirits. Nothing to report.
why: Clipped log, all three at the good end: calm, rested, good spirits.

text: Legs are heavy after the resistance session, pleasantly tired really. Feeling pretty content.
why: Pleasantly tired with heavy legs after exercise = a bit to moderately tired; 'content' is the mood 4 anchor word and 'pretty' rules out 5.

text: No real pressure today, but I'm homesick and pretty miserable tonight.
why: No real pressure = low stress; homesick and pretty miserable = low to very unhappy. Calm but low.
